<objective>
Re-skin the auth route group — signup, login, password reset and their three client components — onto the
Cena design system, at the 44px touch floor, without moving a single behaviour.

Purpose: SC3 names eight surfaces that must render in the new system and be usable one-handed on a phone.
This plan covers three of them. The auth surfaces are the highest-risk group in the phase for reasons that
have nothing to do with appearance: `COPY.errors.auth` is a single shared string whose ambiguity is
account-enumeration resistance; the consent gate has a documented ordering that keeps consent ahead of the
session; and `GoogleOneTap.tsx` holds the one external origin SC1's allowlist permits.

Output: six re-skinned files, all glyphs on the `Icon` wrapper, no behavioural diff.

**Enabling relationship:** this plan delivers no requirement ID. It is one third of SC3.

**The primitives already carry the visual change.** Plans 01.1-05, 01.1-07 and 01.1-08 re-skinned all 19.
These six files change **layout, spacing and composition only** — page shells, form rhythm, stacking on a
narrow viewport. If a file needs a colour class of its own, that is a signal the primitive is wrong, not
the surface.
</objective>

  <reversibility rating="reversible">A visual pass over six auth files. No auth logic, no session handling, no recovery-grant behaviour and no string value changes — the three things that would NOT be reversible on this surface (the ambiguous `COPY.errors.auth`, the consent-gate ordering, the one allowlisted third-party origin) are each held byte-identical by a `git diff` or presence gate rather than by care, and the whole `tests/auth` directory gates every task. Reversing is `git revert`.</reversibility>
  <action>
    Layout and spacing only, mobile-first.

    Apply the Cena spacing rhythm: 16px for default element spacing and card padding, 24px for section
    padding, 32px for the page margin at desktop widths. Page titles render at the Display role in
    `--font-serif`; card titles at Heading in `--font-serif`; body copy at Body in `--font-sans`; form
    labels and button text at Label. **Four size roles and two weights, never a third** — if a size seems
    to be missing, the answer is one of the four, not a new one.

    Design for a 320px viewport first and let the layout widen, rather than shrinking a desktop layout.
    SC3's "usable one-handed on a phone" applies to every owner surface, not only the tablet route group.
    Every interactive control inherits the 44px floor from the primitives; verify none is overridden back
    down by a surface-level height class.

    Keep the shell width classes as they are. They resolve correctly only because `app/globals.css` carries
    matching `--max-width-*` and `--min-width-*` shields for every named spacing token — this exact
    resolution order already shipped as a defect once, collapsing a shell to 16px and clipping the login
    form out of both paint and hit-testing. Do not introduce a new named width without adding its shields.

    Change no string. Every user-visible string on these pages comes from `lib/copy.ts`, and both the
    shared auth error and the consent-checkbox label are contract rows. Do not re-order the consent
    checkbox relative to the submit control, and do not re-order the Google affordance relative to the
    consent gate — the documented ordering keeps consent ahead of the session.

    Migrate every glyph on these pages onto the `Icon` wrapper from plan 01.1-07, so it draws at 1.75. The
    glyph identifiers are still imported from `lucide-react` and passed to the wrapper as a prop; what
    changes is that none is rendered as a bare element.
  </action>

  <action>
    Layout and spacing only. These three are already client components; keep them that way and do not
    convert any of them, nor add a client boundary to anything they render into.

    Apply the Cena form rhythm: 8px between a label and its control, 16px between fields, 24px before the
    submit control. Inputs, the submit button and the Google affordance all inherit the 44px floor from the
    primitives — verify none is overridden down by a local height class. Error presentation uses the
    component the plan 01.1-07 reconciliation named; do not run both `field`'s error slot and the existing
    field-error component on the same field.

    **Three things must not move, and each is a security control rather than a style preference.**

    The shared signup and login error is a **single string used for both**, and its vagueness is
    deliberate: distinguishing "no such account" from "wrong password" is account enumeration. Do not split
    it, do not add a more helpful variant, do not soften it in the lexicon re-cut. It stays exactly as
    `lib/copy.ts` holds it.

    The consent gate stays **ahead of** the session: the Google affordance cannot complete before consent is
    recorded. Do not re-order those elements for visual balance. The gate copy and the unavailable-fallback
    copy are both contract rows.

    `GoogleOneTap.tsx` loads the Google Identity Services script. That is the **one** origin SC1's allowlist
    permits, and it carries an ACCT-01 justification. Do not add a second external origin, do not move the
    script to a different loading strategy that changes the request, and do not remove it. Run
    `tests/theme/no-third-party-assets.test.ts` after this file specifically.

    Migrate every glyph on these three files onto the `Icon` wrapper. Each currently imports a spinner
    glyph directly and renders it as a bare element; route it through the wrapper so it draws at 1.75,
    keeping the existing size and animation classes.

    Preserve the submit-spinner and disable-on-submit behaviour exactly. It is the loading state every
    Phase 01 form uses and SC2 depends on it not moving.
  </action>

<threat_model>
**Review level: OWASP ASVS L1.** This is the level appropriate to a phase that changes no auth logic, no authorization boundary and no data path — 01.1 is a visual and vocabulary migration, and every plan that touches a security-relevant file holds it byte-identical under a `git diff` gate rather than reviewing it. **Block on: `high`.** Every threat rated `high` or `critical` carries a `mitigate` disposition with a named, gated implementation; `medium` and `low` may carry `accept` with a stated rationale. The ASVS V2 and V7 chapters named in the register below are out-of-scope-by-contract markers, not review targets — this plan re-skins the auth surface without reviewing it, which is why the gates assert non-change rather than correctness.

## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| anonymous visitor → auth surface | These are the only surfaces an unauthenticated party reaches. Error wording, gate ordering and script origins are all security-relevant here. |
| browser → accounts.google.com | The single external origin the product permits, justified by ACCT-01. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Severity | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-01.1-05 | Information Disclosure | `COPY.errors.auth` split or softened during the visual pass | high | mitigate | The shared string stays byte-identical; asserted by an empty `git diff` on `lib/copy.ts` plus a presence grep at the login call site. `01.1-RESEARCH.md` § Security Domain records it as ASVS V7 enumeration resistance (T-02-01). |
| T-01.1-09 | Spoofing | Consent-gate ordering re-arranged for visual balance | high | mitigate | The documented ordering keeps consent ahead of the session so the Google affordance cannot complete before consent is recorded. Not re-ordered; the existing affordance-coverage tests are run against these files specifically. |
| T-01.1-03 | Information Disclosure | A second third-party origin introduced during the re-skin | high | mitigate | `tests/theme/no-third-party-assets.test.ts` enforces a one-entry allowlist and is run against this file specifically; the origin count is asserted unchanged. |
| T-01.1-35 | Elevation of Privilege | Auth logic changed under cover of a visual pass | high | mitigate | ASVS V2 is out of scope for this phase by contract: no auth logic, no session handling and no recovery-grant behaviour is touched. Changes are limited to layout, spacing and glyph routing, and the whole `tests/auth` directory gates each task. |
</threat_model>
